podcast.body: The album cover featured John Denver and his wife, Annie, on what looked like a farm, visually catering to country audiences, despite the LP being recorded in Los Angeles. This LP topped both the pop and country album charts, spending one week at number one on the pop chart and an impressive 13 weeks at number one on the country chart. In late summer and fall of 1974, it frequently alternated with Olivia Newton-John's 'If You Love Me, Let Me Know' album at the country chart's top spot. "On the cover of his 1974 album, Back Home Again, John Denver was photographed next to his beloved wife, Annie, straddling a fence on what appeared to be a farm yard."

podcast.body: This album was released in June 1974. Its title track won CMA Song of the Year in 1975, and two other cuts from the album, "Annie's Song" and "Thank God I'm a Country Boy," became two of Denver's biggest hits. "In June 1974, Denver released the Back Home Again album, The Title Track, one song of the year at the CMA's in 1975."
